newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhstan turns back on customs union with Russia.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhstan turns back on customs union with Russia.

text.p: Kazakhstan will turn its back on a customs union with Russia and other former Soviet neighbours because it threatens the country's economic development, a senior customs official said on Tuesday.
"We cannot allow our borders to be as open as they have been until now," Gani Kasymov, chairman of the State Customs Committee, told a news conference.
"The economic security of our state is suffering , huge amounts of contraband goods are being brought in," he said.
Kazakhstan, with a large population of ethnic Russians and reliant on Russian pipelines for oil exports, is normally extremely cautious in its relations with the Kremlin.

Diplomats based in Almaty say Kazakhstan, up for possible membership in the World Trade Organisation (WTO) in June, would prefer Russia to withdraw from the customs union first so as not to be seen as the cause of its collapse.
"There is no point carrying out internal economic reforms if the length and breadth of our borders are porous," Kasymov said.
He said the other members of the customs union -- Russia, Belarus and Kyrgyzstan -- had not kept to the union's strictures, which in turn entitled Kazakhstan to turn its back on it.
"Our neighbours in all geographical directions are strengthening their own borders -- (their) customs posts are now armed with armoured vehicles" said Kasymov.

He said Kazakhstan would start by tightening its customs regime at the country's 19 airports followed by the establishment of customs posts along its lengthy border. The republic of 16.9 million is roughly the size of western Europe.
